assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale evidence on intergenerational mobility has transformed how economists measure equality of opportunity and evaluate places and policies.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are central to the empirical mobility programme, with Katz an important collaborator on its foundational opportunity research.
assessment.maturity: The research agenda has produced a large, influential body of work and durable public-data infrastructure over many years.
uncertainties: The appropriate division of credit among the wider mobility research network is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work gave a compelling account of how technology, tasks, and trade shocks reshape local labour markets and wage inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson provide a coherent and identifiable body of work linking trade exposure and changing labour demand to distributional outcomes.
assessment.maturity: Its empirical designs, concepts, and policy influence have been extensively developed and tested over a long period.
uncertainties: The relative contribution of trade, technology, and other concurrent forces remains contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on health shocks, early environments, and skill formation established the lasting economic importance of conditions early in life.
assessment.attribution: Currie and Almond are especially associated with credible empirical evidence on early-life conditions, while Cunha is central to the dynamic skill-formation framework.
assessment.maturity: The findings are supported by a broad accumulated literature and have substantially shaped education, health, and social-policy research.
uncertainties: The candidate grouping spans complementary empirical and theoretical contributions rather than a single discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods made possible credible analysis of persistent behaviour with short panels and endogenous regressors across applied economics.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond are the clearest originators of the core estimator, with Blundell central to its system-GMM extension.
assessment.maturity: These methods are mature, highly influential, and their strengths and limitations are now well understood.
uncertainties: Routine use of the methods has sometimes exceeded the strength of available instruments.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification redirected empirical practice toward conclusions warranted by weak and transparent assumptions rather than unwarranted point identification.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the principal intellectual architect, and Tamer made central contributions to moment-inequality methods.
assessment.maturity: The framework is well established theoretically and increasingly consequential in applied work where identification is limited.
uncertainties: Its broad practical influence is less visible than that of some point-estimation methods.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern analysis of monopsony has changed economists' understanding of wage setting, employer power, and the incidence of labour-market policy.
assessment.attribution: Manning supplied the most coherent foundational synthesis and theoretical framework for the modern monopsony literature.
assessment.maturity: Subsequent empirical work has made employer market power a central and durable issue in labour economics.
uncertainties: The empirical extent and mechanisms of monopsony vary substantially across settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The combination of theory and measurement of selection in insurance markets has materially improved understanding of insurance design and welfare.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein, Einav, and Salanie each made influential contributions connecting selection theory to credible empirical measurement.
assessment.maturity: The programme is mature and has generated extensive applications in health, credit, and other insurance markets.
uncertainties: Attribution must distinguish the broad insurance-selection literature from the particular empirical programme.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence designs provided unusually direct evidence on labour-market discrimination and changed empirical research and policy debate.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are strongly associated with landmark modern field evidence; Charles is also an important contributor to the wider literature.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been replicated and extended across countries and markets for decades.
uncertainties: Audit studies identify important treatment differences but do not by themselves fully establish all mechanisms behind discrimination.
